deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues Riemann's treatment of minimal surfaces bounded by straight lines, some of which may run to infinity. This is the material Hattendorff edited as 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Göttingen 13, 1867).

Ingredients from the previous page:
- eta is the stereographic image of the Gauss map.
- u is defined by du = sqrt(i dx / d log eta) d log eta. In modern terms du^2 is, up to a constant factor, the Hopf (second fundamental form) quadratic differential.
- Along a straight boundary segment du is either real or purely imaginary, so du^2 is real.
- t is a conformal parameter mapping the surface once onto the upper half-plane Im t > 0, with the boundary going to the real axis.

Step 1: catalogue of the special points.
(a) t = a_1, a_2, ...: umbilic points.
- Riemann describes them three ways: branch points of the Gauss image on the sphere; points where the tangent plane cuts the surface in more than two curves (n curves, n >= 3; n = 3 is a simple branch point); and 'Krümmungsradius = ∞' (principal curvatures zero).
- They may lie in the interior or on the boundary. A boundary one is a point where the tangent plane meets the surface in further curves besides the boundary line.
(b) t = b_1, b_2, ...: corners of the polygonal boundary.
(c) t = c_1, c_2, ...: ends of the surface running to infinity, between two boundary lines.

Step 2: local behaviour, in modern form.
- d/dt log(du/dt) = (n/2 - 1)/(t - a) + holomorphic near t = a. That is, du/dt ~ (t - a)^{n/2 - 1}.
- du/dt ~ (t - b)^{m/2 - 1} near a corner b. For m = 1 one gets u ~ (t - b)^{1/2}, so the half-plane maps to a quarter-plane: the image angle in the u-plane is a multiple m·π/2. A regular boundary point corresponds to m = 2.
- u = sqrt(alpha/(2π)) log(t - c) + holomorphic near an end c. This maps a neighbourhood of c in the half-plane onto a half-strip in the u-plane; alpha is a width parameter of the end.
- Elsewhere u is finite and continuous.
- Riemann adds: for a not real (interior umbilics), the conjugate points must also be understood among the a's. This anticipates the reflection.

Step 3: reflection.
- On the real t-axis dt is real and du is real or purely imaginary, so (du/dt)^2 is real there.
- It continues analytically across the real axis by assigning to the conjugate point t' = conj(t) the conjugate value (Schwarz reflection).
- Hence (du/dt)^2 is single-valued on the whole t-plane. By the local data it is meromorphic with only finitely many poles, so it is rational.

Step 4: reduction to simple cases.
- It suffices to take n = 3 and m = 1. The general case arises by letting points coalesce.
- A boundary umbilic of order n > 3 is (n - 2) simple branch points merged.
- A corner with m > 1 is a corner with m = 1 merged with (m - 1) simple branch points.

Step 5: result.
(du/dt)^2 = C · Π(t - a) / (Π(t - b) · Π(t - c)^2), with real coefficients, i.e.
u = const · ∫ sqrt(Π(t - a)/Π(t - b)) dt / Π(t - c) + const.
Here Π(t - a) runs over boundary simple branch points and interior simple branch points together with their conjugates.

Step 6: conditions on the constants.
- The constants a, b, c (and C) must be chosen so that near each c the coefficient of log(t - c) is sqrt(A/(2π)); A here is the alpha above. This is a residue condition.
- For u to stay finite and continuous at all t other than a, b, c, which concerns t = ∞, a relation among the numbers of these points must hold.
- My completion: if t = ∞ is an ordinary boundary point, then with s = -1/t we need du/ds = t^2 du/dt regular and nonzero. So (du/dt)^2 ~ t^{-4}, giving
  N_b + 2 N_c - N_a(boundary) - 2 N_a(interior) = 4.
- The next page states this counting relation in words.

Overall: this is a Schwarz–Christoffel-type representation of the Hopf-differential coordinate u for polygonal minimal surfaces.
errors: Written 'du = sqrt(...) dt/Π(t-c) const + const'. The additive constant belongs to u = ∫ ... + const, not to du; this is a notational slip.

Π(t-a) must include the conjugates of interior branch points, which Riemann says in words but does not show in the formula. It must also include boundary branch points and the extra factors coming from corners with m > 1 (via coalescence).

The condition at t = ∞ is not written out on this page. It is only alluded to ('a relation must hold') and given in words on the next page. As transcribed there, the order of the 'double difference' seems reversed relative to the degree count N_b - N_a,bd = 4 + 2(N_a,int - N_c). This needs checking against the image of the next page.
Notation drifts between alpha and A for the end parameter.
The relation between m and the actual spatial corner angle is not stated; m only fixes the angle mπ/2 in the u-plane. This is not an error but is left implicit.

results.what: Representation (du/dt)^2 = C Π(t-a)/(Π(t-b) Π(t-c)^2) for minimal surfaces bounded by straight lines, after mapping to a half-plane and reflecting
results.modern_name: Schwarz–Christoffel-type formula for the Hopf differential / Weierstrass data of polygonal minimal surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous 1867, ed. Hattendorff); independently Weierstrass (1866) and H. A. Schwarz (1865–1871)

results.what: Continuation of (du/dt)^2 across the real axis by assigning conjugate values at conjugate points
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1870); Riemann's use is known from his minimal surface memoir

results.what: Local exponents at umbilics (n/2 - 1), corners (m/2 - 1) and infinite ends (logarithmic); reduction of higher-order points to coalesced simple ones
results.modern_name: Local normal forms of the Hopf differential at umbilics and polygon corners

results.what: Counting relation among corners, ends and branch points from the behaviour at t = ∞ (completed on the next page)
results.modern_name: Degree / Gauss–Bonnet-type index count for the quadratic differential

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material that appears in Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface memoir (1867). The method — half-plane uniformization, reflection, and a Schwarz–Christoffel-type integral for u — is known to be his. The only extra value is the draft-level detail, such as the coalescence argument and the geometric description of umbilics.

checkable.asserts: For m = 1, u ~ (t-b)^(1/2) gives (du/dt)^2 with a simple pole at b, i.e. a factor 1/(t-b) (constant 1/4).
log(du/dt) = (n/2 - 1) log(t-a) + regular has logarithmic derivative (n/2 - 1)/(t-a); for n = 3, du/dt ~ (t-a)^(1/2).
Near an infinite end, (du/dt)^2 has a double pole with coefficient alpha/(2*pi).

checkable.sympy: t,s=symbols('t s'); b=symbols('b1:5'); R=1/prod([t-bi for bi in b]); limit(R.subs(t,-1/s)*(1/s**2)**2, s, 0)
checkable.asserts: With four m = 1 corners and nothing else, (du/ds)^2 = R(t) t^4 has a finite nonzero limit at t = ∞ (it equals 1), so t = ∞ is a regular boundary point. This is the skew-quadrilateral case.
Degree condition for (du/dt)^2 ~ t^(-4) at infinity: denominator degree minus numerator degree equals 4.
Crossing t = c along the real axis, Im u jumps by sqrt(alpha/(2*pi))*pi, the width of the image half-strip.

transcription_corrections: Heading: the first word likely begins 'Bestimmung ...' rather than 'Erweiterung'; the line is uncertain.
Last lines: 'eine Relation zwischen den Argumenten dieser Werthe' should more plausibly read 'zwischen den Anzahlen dieser Werthe'. This fits the counting relation on the next page.
'Wir begreifen darunter den Fall, wo in der Begrenzung die Tangentialebene die Fläche in mehr als einer geraden Linie schneidet': the 'nach einem' in the transcription is spurious.
The marginal note continues 'unter a die obigen a, und wenn sie nicht reell sind, ihre conjugirten zu verstehen sind' (the conjugates are to be included as well).
The marginal 'Speciell fallen wenn n>3 (n-2) einfache Verzweigungspunkte in einen [Punkt] zusammen und wenn m>1 (m-1) einfache Verzweigungspunkte in eine Ecke [?]' gives the coalescence statement.
In the final formula the second constant should be read as belonging to u (u = ∫ ... + const). The constant in the residue condition is written 'A' (= alpha above).
